items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 22 at 2:49PM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
Minor coastal erosion and high surf conditions are expected for
parts of the West Coast as a Bering Sea low passes by Sunday
through early Tuesday. Primarily South to Southeast wind
directions could help water levels reach 2-4 feet above the mean
high tide level. No flooding is expected.
items.areas: Lower Kobuk Valley; Baldwin Peninsula; Northern Seward Peninsula; Shishmaref; Bering Strait Coast; Southern Seward Peninsula Coast; Eastern Norton Sound and Nulato Hills; Yukon Delta Coast

items.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 22 at 2:05PM AKST until November 24 at 12:00AM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...High Water Levels 2 to 4 feet above the normal high
tide line.

* WHERE...Eastern Norton Sound and Nulato Hills.

* WHEN...Until midnight AKST Monday night.

* IMPACTS...Localized beach erosion may occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The highest water levels will coincide
with periods of high tide.
items.areas: Eastern Norton Sound and Nulato Hills
items.instruction: Precautions should be taken to protect property.

items.headline: Dense Fog Advisory issued November 22 at 1:34PM AKST until November 23 at 9:00AM AKST by NWS Juneau AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Visibility of 1/4 mile at times in dense fog.

* WHERE...City and Borough of Juneau.

* WHEN...Until 9 AM AKST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Low visibility could make travel conditions hazardous.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Dense fog is persisting near the Juneau
airport and in the Mendenhall Valley.
items.instruction:
If driving, slow down, use your headlights, and leave plenty of
distance ahead of you.

items.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 22 at 1:00PM AKST until November 25 at 9:00AM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Blowing snow expected. Winds gusting as high as 40 mph.

* WHERE...Central Beaufort Sea Coast and Eastern Beaufort Sea Coast.

* WHEN...From 9 AM Monday to 9 AM AKST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Blowing snow could reduce
visibility below one half mile at times.
items.areas: Central Beaufort Sea Coast; Eastern Beaufort Sea Coast
items.instruction: Use caution while traveling, especially in open areas.

items.headline: Air Quality Alert issued November 22 at 12:46PM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
The Department of Environmental Conservation has issued an Air
Quality Alert which is IN EFFECT UNTIL 2 PM AKST MONDAY.

North Pole has a Stage 2 alert.

Fairbanks has no alert.

items.headline: High Wind Warning issued November 22 at 12:31PM AKST until November 23 at 9:00AM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Southeast winds 30 to 40 mph with gusts up to 60 mph
expected.

* WHERE...St Lawrence Island.

* WHEN...From 6 PM this evening to 9 AM AKST Monday.

* IMPACTS...High winds may move loose debris, damage property & cause
power outages. Travel could be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The strongest wind gusts will be Sunday
evening & Sunday night.
items.instruction:
People are urged to secure loose objects that could be blown around
or damaged by the wind.

items.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 22 at 2:57AM AKST until November 23 at 3:00AM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Elevated coastal water levels of 1 to 2 feet above the
normal highest tide line.

* WHERE...Coastal Kuskokwim Delta Communities, including Kipnuk,
Kongiganak, and Kwigillingok.

* WHEN...3 AM Sunday to 3 AM AKST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Elevated coastal water levels driven by southeast
winds gusting to 55 mph. Coastal erosion is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Gusty southeasterly winds will begin
increasing early Sunday morning as the storm approaches.
Highest water levels expected late S
items.areas: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island
items.instruction:
Precautions should be taken to protect property, such as securing
or moving property away from the shoreline.
